items.stem: A student claims that NATO bombing began immediately after the Račak massacre. Identify the error in this claim and correct it.
items.answer: Račak was followed by negotiations at Rambouillet and Paris; bombing began on 24 March 1999, after Belgrade rejected the accords.
items.markingKey: Račak was followed by negotiations at Rambouillet and Paris; bombing began on 24 March 1999, after Belgrade rejected the accords. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem:
Source A: Paraphrased from Ibrahim Rugova, President of the unofficial Republic of Kosova, interview with a foreign journalist, Pristina, 1993

We have chosen the path of peace. We will not give the Serbian regime the excuse it seeks to massacre our people. Our institutions, our schools and our elections show the world that we are ready to govern ourselves.

Source B: Paraphrased from Tim Judah, British journalist and historian, Kosovo: War and Revenge, 2000

Dayton taught Kosovo Albanians a bitter lesson: the world rewards those who fight. Rugova’s peaceful policy had won sympathy but no results, and young men began to listen to those who said only arms could free Kosovo.

Compare and contrast what Sources A and B reveal about Kosovo Albanian resistance to Serbian rule, 1989–1998.
items.answer: Both refer to the strategy of peaceful resistance. Rugova defends non-violence as protecting Albanians and showing their capacity to self-govern, while Judah argues that by 1995 this policy had failed and was being rejected; A defends the strategy, B explains its collapse.
items.markingKey: Both refer to the strategy of peaceful resistance. Rugova defends non-violence as protecting Albanians and showing their capacity to self-govern, while Judah argues that by 1995 this policy had failed and was being rejected; A defends the strategy, B explains its collapse. Award 1 mark per valid, explicitly linked point of comparison or contrast, up to [4]; at least one comparison and one contrast are needed for full marks. A running (integrated) comparison is preferred to end-on description; do not credit points about provenance in this question.

items.stem:
Source A: Slobodan Milošević, President of Serbia, speech at Gazimestan, Kosovo, 28 June 1989 (extract, translation)

Six centuries later, now, we are being again engaged in battles and are facing battles. They are not armed battles, although such things cannot yet be excluded.

Source B: Paraphrased from the draft Memorandum of the Serbian Academy of Sciences and Arts (SANU), leaked to the press in Belgrade, September 1986

The physical, political, legal and cultural genocide of the Serbian population in Kosovo and Metohija is the worst defeat in the liberation struggles that Serbia has waged.

Using the sources and your own knowledge, to what extent do you agree that the break-up of Yugoslavia was caused mainly by the nationalist policies of Slobodan Milošević?
items.answer: Milošević was the single most important actor, but economic crisis and other nationalisms also drove disintegration.
items.markingKey: Indicative content – supporting: Kosovo Polje and the anti-bureaucratic revolution; revocation of Kosovo autonomy; support for Serb rebels in Croatia and Bosnia. Challenging: economic crisis and debt in the 1980s; Slovene and Croatian nationalism (Tuđman); collapse of communism and recognition by the EC. Judgement: Milošević was the single most important actor, but economic crisis and other nationalisms also drove disintegration. Candidates must use both sources and their own knowledge; Markbands – 6–8: focused response; effective use of the sources and accurate own knowledge, integrated (synthesised) to support a clear, balanced judgement; 4–5: some focus on the question; uses sources or own knowledge, with some analysis but little synthesis; 1–3: limited understanding; generalised comments, sources or own knowledge used descriptively; 0: does not reach the standard of the descriptors below.

items.stem:
Source A: Paraphrased from statements by critics of NATO policy, as reported in The Guardian (London), 1999–2000

Rambouillet was not a negotiation. The text was presented to the Serbs as an ultimatum which no sovereign state could accept; it was an excuse to start bombing.

Source B: William Walker, head of the OSCE Kosovo Verification Mission, press conference at Račak, 16 January 1999

From what I personally saw, I do not hesitate to describe the event as a massacre, a crime against humanity. Nor do I hesitate to accuse the government security forces of responsibility.

Using the sources and your own knowledge, discuss the view that NATO intervention in 1999 was the result of Milošević’s refusal to compromise.
items.answer: Milošević’s policies made intervention likely, but NATO’s terms and interests also shaped the outcome.
items.markingKey: Indicative content – supporting: repeated breaches of the October 1998 agreement; Račak massacre; rejection of Rambouillet. Challenging: Appendix B was arguably unacceptable to any state; KLA provocations escalated the conflict; NATO credibility and US interests. Judgement: Milošević’s policies made intervention likely, but NATO’s terms and interests also shaped the outcome. items.stem: Which event of 1997 provided the KLA with large quantities of weapons?
options: NATO arms deliveries
The collapse of the Albanian state after pyramid schemes failed
The fall of the Berlin Wall
The Dayton Agreement
items.answer: The collapse of the Albanian state after pyramid schemes failed
items.markingKey: B. Looting of army depots in Albania released hundreds of thousands of weapons.

items.stem: Which term matches this description: "The mass rallies of 1988–1989 organised by Milošević’s supporters that toppled the leaderships of Vojvodina, Kosovo and Montenegro"?
options: Kosovo Verification Mission (KVM)
1974 Constitution
passive resistance
anti-bureaucratic revolution
items.answer: anti-bureaucratic revolution
items.markingKey: D. This is the definition of anti-bureaucratic revolution.

items.stem: Distinguish between the Rambouillet proposals of 1999 and the Holbrooke–Milošević agreement of October 1998.
items.answer: The October agreement relied on unarmed OSCE monitors and partial withdrawal; Rambouillet proposed autonomy guaranteed by a NATO-led military force, which Belgrade saw as occupation.
items.markingKey: The October agreement relied on unarmed OSCE monitors and partial withdrawal; Rambouillet proposed autonomy guaranteed by a NATO-led military force, which Belgrade saw as occupation. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: Diego writes: "The KLA was a large, well-organised army when it first appeared in 1996." Explain why this is inaccurate.
items.answer: It began as small, loosely organised cells; it grew rapidly only after the Drenica massacres of 1998 brought mass recruitment.
items.markingKey: It began as small, loosely organised cells; it grew rapidly only after the Drenica massacres of 1998 brought mass recruitment. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: A student claims that Kosovo was one of the six republics of Yugoslavia. Identify the error in this claim and correct it.
items.answer: Kosovo was an autonomous province within Serbia, not a republic, though the 1974 constitution gave it near-republican powers.
items.markingKey: Kosovo was an autonomous province within Serbia, not a republic, though the 1974 constitution gave it near-republican powers. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Explain why the Račak massacre was a turning point in Western policy towards Kosovo.
items.answer: Graphic reports of executed civilians, verified by OSCE monitors, convinced Western governments that Milošević could not be trusted and led directly to the Rambouillet ultimatum.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Graphic reports of executed civilians, verified by OSCE monitors, convinced Western governments that Milošević could not be trusted and led directly to the Rambouillet ultimatum. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Explain why the creation of parallel institutions was significant.
items.answer: After Albanians were dismissed from state jobs and schools, the parallel system preserved education and health care and built a de facto Albanian state rejecting Serbian authority.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: After Albanians were dismissed from state jobs and schools, the parallel system preserved education and health care and built a de facto Albanian state rejecting Serbian authority. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Briefly describe the Kosovo Polje meeting of 24 April 1987 and explain what it reveals about the role of individual leaders in nationalist mobilisation.
items.answer: Serb demonstrators clashed with police; Milošević declared “no one should dare to beat you!”, broadcast on television. The moment transformed a party official into a nationalist leader and showed how elites could exploit grievances.
items.markingKey: Context (Serb demonstrators clashed with police; Milošević declared “no one should dare to beat you!”, broadcast on television.) – 1 mark for accurate, specific detail. Link: The moment transformed a party official into a nationalist leader and showed how elites could exploit grievances. – remaining marks for explicitly connecting the example to the role of individual leaders in nationalist mobilisation.

items.answer: Kosovo was an autonomous province within Serbia, not a republic, though the 1974 constitution gave it near-republican powers.

items.stem: Outline one way in which Appendix B of the Rambouillet Accords shows the debate over whether Rambouillet was a genuine negotiation.
items.answer: It allowed NATO personnel unrestricted passage throughout the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. Critics argue it was designed to be unacceptable to Belgrade, justifying bombing; defenders say it was standard status-of-forces language.
items.markingKey: Context (It allowed NATO personnel unrestricted passage throughout the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia.) – 1 mark for accurate, specific detail. Link: Critics argue it was designed to be unacceptable to Belgrade, justifying bombing; defenders say it was standard status-of-forces language. – remaining marks for explicitly connecting the example to the debate over whether Rambouillet was a genuine negotiation.

items.stem: Give one argument for and one argument against the view that the rise of the KLA was due mainly to the failure of the international community to address Kosovo at Dayton.
items.answer: Dayton discredited non-violence, but repression and the availability of weapons turned frustration into an armed movement.
items.markingKey: Arguments for: Dayton ignored Kosovo; non-violence produced no results; Albanians concluded that force was rewarded. Arguments against: Serbian repression and dismissals; weapons from Albania in 1997; diaspora funding and radical nationalism; Prekaz massacre 1998. Supported judgement: Dayton discredited non-violence, but repression and the availability of weapons turned frustration into an armed movement.
